text:
maria: Quick flag — our rollout heatmap shows a short spike of attributed streaming tokens to the canary model yesterday at 04:12 UTC even though most traffic should have been routed to stable. noticed while digging quotas.
maria: snippet from router logs: `route=canary fallback=stable req=abc123 tokens_charged=482` — looks like a mid-request model swap and the ledger kept the canary attribution.
chris: ugh. do we have repro steps? is this the same path as the session-handoff bug from last month?
maria: not identical. last month was prefix ownership; this feels like attribution tag not being updated on the handoff. happens when streaming chunk boundary coincides with a model downgrade.
leo: @maria can you paste the query you used to surface the heatmap? want to check if console is double-counting or ledger actually shows the token rows.
maria: sure — quick query: ```sql
SELECT route, sum(tokens) FROM token_ledger WHERE time > '2025-02-14' AND req_id = 'abc123' GROUP BY 1;
``` results showed tokens split 70/30 canary/stable but runtime traces show final response from stable.
dev-bot: alert: routing-canary-rate > threshold — incident created (#INC-4021)
chris: hypothesis: when we do model-swap mid-stream we tag outgoing chunks with the current model id but ledger write for the earlier provisional chunks may be updated by a reconciler that doesn't reconcile the routing_tag. So UI reads reconciler rows + provisional rows => spike.
ewa: can we add a short-lived telemetry tag like `final_route` on confirm path so the console aggregates by final_route if present? then the heatmap would show accurate attribution during rollouts.
leo: good call. short-term fix: modify the aggregator to prefer `final_route` if present, fall back to `initial_route` otherwise. lower risk than changing router writes.
maria: agree. i'll open an RFC for this change and attach the query + failing trace. cc @chris @leo
chris: if you can include a small dashboard patch (rename metric -> routed_model_final) we can ship as a canary quick fix.
maria: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
